label: Essence as nature or quiddity: Essence is what a thing is, its nature or quiddity, contrasted with…
term: essence as nature or quiddity (Thomistic attribute readings)
definition: Essence is what a thing is, its nature or quiddity, contrasted with its act of being (esse). The statement that God is his own esse identifies these in its theological context; the words essence and esse alone do not make that identity hold. This sense is not Scott’s modal essence of an individual or the 1970 Gödel variant’s different essence definition.
note: A terminological stipulation for the existing attribute records, checked against the materialized q.3 a.4 contrast of what a thing is with its esse. No new Lean essence predicate or identity proof is introduced; sourcing a general essence theory remains separate from this vocabulary link. Lean locator: PrimaPars.Question3.Article4.Profile.essenceOf : Being → Principle is an existing primitive representation of nature, with the separately supplied esseOf field. Generic q.3/q.11 readings also take essenceOf as a parameter of that type. The field fixes neither a general essence theory nor the identity of essence and esse; those interpretive applications and open identity premises remain separate.

formal_gap.meaning: Profile.essenceOf x is x's essence: what x is, its nature or quiddity, represented as an element of the shared Principle sort so that it can be compared with x's act of being, esseOf x. A q.3 a.4 profile supplies the map; Lean fixes only that each being has one essence principle, and that 'essence differs from esse' means esseOf x ≠ essenceOf x in that sort.
examples: The humanity of Socrates, as what Socrates is, contrasted with his act of being.
In q.3 a.4 a being whose esse differs from its essence (DistinctEsseAt) is the case the first proof says has its esse caused by another.
exclusions: Scott's and Gödel's modal essences of an individual (DEF-ESSENCE-SCOTT, DEF-ESSENCE-GOEDEL-1970): different definitions, kept apart in DISAMB-ESSENCE.
The act of being (esseOf): a separate field; their identity in God is the open statement STMT-GOD-IS-HIS-OWN-ESSE, not a consequence of the words.
open_obligations: No general theory of essence is supplied; that Principle identity tracks real identity of essence and esse is an interpretive application that remains OPEN.
Whether every being has exactly one essence principle in the intended sense is assumed by the function type rather than argued.
No formalization candidate from existing vocabulary.
